purpose: Test whether sequentially safe-resolving both players at every reached flop root can improve the two-iteration continual-resolving leader while protecting each updated player against the complete two-iteration flop anchor.

comparison.interpretation: The bilateral flop update moved responder-zero values in both directions and worsened their paired mean. Both responder-one values remained unchanged to less than 1.3e-10bb, so the dominant responder-one leak on these frozen samples is outside the causal reach of this flop policy intervention. Do not spend more compute increasing bilateral flop iterations from this branch.

implementationEvidence.atomicity: The complete projected policy for both players is installed as one cache generation; missing protected flop descendants fail closed.
implementationEvidence.safety: Each sequential player update is projected toward its complete anchor until the exact maximum opponent counterfactual-value excess is at most 0.05bb per compatible private hand.
implementationEvidence.routing: Safe routing serves the projected generation for either actor throughout the protected flop subtree and isolates resolver caches between evaluator workers.
implementationEvidence.validation: The policy-only safe solve is byte-equivalent to the full diagnostic solve for the deployed actor, and the integration regression reaches and serves both actors from one bilateral generation.

releaseGate.reason: The two-deal directional mean is above the release gate and worse than the validated leader. Two deals are not sufficient evidence for a release confidence bound.

nextExperiment: Trace the frozen information-set best response's selected preflop actions and reached street for the unchanged responder-one values, then change the causally responsible policy actions. Retain the 1.4127416606284693 leader and keep activation disabled.
